checks.finding: The design supplies rationale for its architectural and technology choices: the transactional publisher addresses the explicitly identified limit of per-target atomic renames (specs/epic-189-a1-project-context/design.md:358); resolved registry, classification-array and Phase-2 decisions and the stdlib-only restricted YAML parser have stated reasons and alternatives (design.md:1475). The RT002 adapter retains the existing verifier and wrappers, explicitly limits transcript matching to content binding, and explains why fresh trusted-session dispatch remains necessary (design.md:15, design.md:59).

No unresolved implementation-blocking question remains in the Open Questions section. OQ-001 and OQ-002 are expressly resolved by the preceding design decisions; OQ-003 is resolved by following the repository Phase model (specs/epic-189-a1-project-context/design.md:1861, design.md:1475). Their continued identifiers are historical resolution references, not ownerless open decisions.

The assumptions identify investigation-backed guard inventory and exact-match behavior, require task-start re-verification of shared generated state, and ground runtime-denial assumptions in INV-015 with re-verification through Risks (specs/epic-189-a1-project-context/design.md:1837). The approved-snapshot assumption is an explicit internal publisher contract with a documented missing/corrupted-snapshot failure mode, rather than an unsupported git-history assumption. The RT002 amendment expressly supersedes the former Codex plugin_hooks prerequisite and requires current installed-verifier and host verification (design.md:65, design.md:75).

Constraint Compliance addresses the requirement constraints covering schemas, canonicalization, HMAC and identity binding, protected publication, weakening provenance, guard behavior, compatibility, wrappers and CI portability (specs/epic-189-a1-project-context/design.md:1803). The RT002 design explicitly adopts requirements.md and acceptance-tests.md as normative for schema dispatch, exact response matching, rejection categories and cleanup, and identifies the retained historical passages it supersedes (design.md:5, design.md:47). The authorized AC-028 resolution supplies the governing shared-CI policy (design.md:1970), consistent with the corresponding infra/security amendments rather than silently allowing their historical summaries to override the revised contract.
No performance requirements found in requirements.md.

The deployment plan identifies local repository tooling, no runtime deployment or new plugin, shell/PowerShell suite integration, deterministic offline CI evidence and explicit handling of already-human-applied protected changes during rollback (specs/epic-189-a1-project-context/design.md:1781). The dated AC-028 resolution governs shared-CI application, preserving existing checks and requiring fresh source verification instead of publishing an old workflow snapshot (design.md:1970). No incremental service rollout or database migration requires a feature flag or database/application deployment order.

Data Plan defines repository YAML/JSON documents and approval artifacts, not database tables or columns, so the database migration-file and row-volume conditions do not apply (specs/epic-189-a1-project-context/design.md:389). The file-contract transition is nevertheless addressed by migration strategy and by the explicit existing-file validation versus absent-file compatibility behavior (design.md:529, design.md:1803); protected-state rollback obligations are recorded in Deployment / CI Plan (design.md:1781).

The scope introduces no external network service or provider API integration; provider bindings remain a skeleton contract. Native host integrations are identified through the hook-activation CLI contract and its runtime-specific recorded-evidence predicates (specs/epic-189-a1-project-context/design.md:626, design.md:1177). The RT002 amendment specifies the Codex schema selector, runtime agreement, exact nonce/envelope checks and fail-closed diagnostics (design.md:15). Deterministic CI explicitly excludes network, gh and LLM invocation and assigns live cross-runtime proof to A8 (design.md:1781).

Architecture and Components map the schemas, canonicalizer, signer/validator, weakening detector, protected publication, track selection and host handshake to REQ-001 through REQ-011 (specs/epic-189-a1-project-context/design.md:135, design.md:212). Supporting approver-registry and transactional-publisher artifacts are justified by existing approval and multi-target publication requirements (design.md:358). RT002 limits its amendment to REQ-010 / AC-027 / AC-032, and the separately identified AC-028 resolution remains within the authorized CI repair; neither claims A8 live acceptance or broader integration completion (design.md:5, design.md:75, design.md:1970).

Test Strategy names concrete planned evidence for parser/canonical bytes, HMAC mutations and identity checks, weakening classification, protected inventory, mutation denial, publication failure recovery and compatibility consumers (specs/epic-189-a1-project-context/design.md:1235). RT002 adds explicit original-path regression coverage for exact emitted bytes, missing/extra/duplicate members, type/runtime/schema faults, nonce/envelope mutations, legacy behavior, cleanup and sidecar non-mutation; it also requires persisted mismatch-test preflight and fresh installed-path live evidence before activation (design.md:75). These are concrete verification paths, not claims that this read-only review executed them or completed a quality gate.
